intro: A record of what presently has my attention.

music.title: Warm Safe Place
music.note: The harmonization at “and then I find you here” is like bliss.
interest: My musical interests are eclectic, but a recent attempt to name the genre of some new music turned into a deeper conversation about why it resonates with me. I realized that I’m drawn less to depressive themes than to a dreamy, isolated atmosphere—a mixture of shoegaze, ambient, slowcore, and horror.

That led me to mono no aware, the Japanese idea of finding beauty in impermanence. I made a playlist and an eerie cover around that feeling, with a solitary figure representing the shadow impermanence casts over life. A great deal of the music, art, and philosophy I love seems to revolve around finding beauty in things precisely because they cannot last.

screen.title: Se7en
screen.plot: Two detectives, a rookie and a veteran, hunt a serial killer who uses the seven deadly sins as his motives.
screen.awards: Nominated for 1 Oscar; 29 wins and 44 nominations total.
notes: TikTok said this movie had a plot twist, so I finally got around to watching it. It became one of the highest-scored movies in my Obsidian vault.

I thought Se7en was good, and the conversation in the car near the end was probably my favorite part. The ending is poetic, but it did not hit nearly as hard as it could have because the emotional buildup was not there. The envy and wrath parts felt rushed, and the movie could have been much stronger if it had developed certain characters more.
One of the major investigative breakthroughs also felt like such an unrealistic leap that it genuinely annoyed me. I have no idea why the IMDb rating is that high—I’d give it around a 7.

screen.title: Two and a Half Men
screen.plot: A hedonistic jingle writer’s free-wheeling life comes to an abrupt halt when his brother and 10-year-old nephew move into his beach-front house.
screen.awards: Won 9 Primetime Emmys; 30 wins and 73 nominations total.
notes: I saw the show off and on at home while growing up. I started the series again to have something on in the background, and I love it. After watching the Charlie Sheen documentary, Charlie has been on my mind; almost immediately, he also reminded me of an older version of Drake Bell from Drake & Josh.
Season 9 is when Ashton Kutcher joins, so I plan to stop after Season 8. I really hate how they killed off Charlie.
S1E18: so funny. A great episode. Joke after joke. It is also funny how Alan is always making pros-and-cons lists—it becomes a recurring, very Type A bit.

presently.label: Working on
presently.text: I’m developing a stronger structure for my PhD so I can triage data and become more organized. I really like the program, but it is difficult because it requires doing many things simultaneously. I’m trying to use systems to stay sane, efficient, and capable of working at a high level. I have high standards for myself, and I do not want to compromise them simply because I am stretched thin.

presently.label: Reading
presently.text: A collection of PhD and graduate-school writing books. I think I understand the greater themes now; the next step is to execute and follow through on them. Eventually, I would also love to build a bookshelf of what I have read on this site.

presently.label: Recent discovery
presently.text: Liza Minnelli’s mother is Judy Garland.

presently.label: Looking forward to
presently.text: An upcoming trip to South Carolina at the end of August.

presently.label: One open question
presently.text: I’m so caught up in the immediate act of doing at this point in my career. I wonder whether everything I’m doing now will eventually pay off in the future.
